[LUNI.13.5.2] **No implicit rounding.** Any expression producing a
fractional-currency intermediate (`Float × currency`, `currency / Float`, FX
conversion) must be wrapped in an explicit `.round("<mode>")` *before*
assignment to a currency slot, comparison against a currency slot, or use as an
`emit`-action argument typed as currency. Compile error:
`DS_VALIDATE_CURRENCY_IMPLICIT_ROUND`.

**`is` / `is not` ([LNUL.4.9]) is not a fourth position.**

The three positions above share a property the tag test does not: each
**consumes the value** — stores it, compares its magnitude, or ships it — so a
rounding the author did not write would change what is stored, matched or sent.
A tag test consumes only the discriminant, and reads it **before any value
conversion** ([LNUL.4.9]), so there is no implicit rounding for it to be
implicit about.

An unrounded fractional-currency intermediate is a `Ratio`, and a `Ratio`
answers `false` to all six tag names ([LNUL.4.9]). That is the true answer
about the value in hand, not a silently wrong one: the author who asks whether
an unrounded intermediate is an `Int` is told that it is not. Refusing the
spelling would make `is` the one operator forbidden to observe a
representation the language admits.
gap_reason: The COMPARISON position has neither an implementation nor a vector. DS_VALIDATE_CURRENCY_IMPLICIT_ROUND is raised from one site only, _check_emit_publish_kwargs, and all three conformance ties drive an emit -- so the clause reads as covered while one of the three positions it names is unexercised. Asserted so the gap is visible instead of implied by the absence of a vector nobody thought to write ([STYL.5.10.8]).
